A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mirage study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original federated-learning experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and GTSRB, including attack comparisons, persistence evaluations, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds mixed-method attacker-conflict results and numerical patched-trigger performance in its appendices.

M1.justification: The adversarial detector-based trigger optimization, mapping-enhancement objective, and local poisoning procedure remain unchanged. Equations 1–3 and Algorithm 1 receive notation and explanation edits, including renaming the trigger learning-rate symbol, without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a heterogeneous adversarial environment with Vanilla, Chameleon, and Neurotoxin attackers operating together, extending the earlier same-method conflict illustration. Dataset and image-classification coverage remain unchanged; patched triggers were already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: Mirage retains the same five attack comparators and six evaluated defenses in Table 1, and the persistence and distribution comparisons retain their methods. The new mixed-method conflict experiment does not evaluate an additional comparator against Mirage; newly cited defenses are not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: The added conflict diagnostic uses three distinct attack methods, whereas the retained Figure 1 illustrates two Vanilla attackers. This adds an evaluation configuration without revising the existing experiments' splits, metrics, architectures, or budgets. Newly disclosed target labels do not establish a setting change.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 tests whether conflict persists when attackers use different algorithms, adding ASR curves in Figure 7. Appendix E also supplements the existing patched-trigger robustness analysis with quantitative performance. The original enhancement ablation and sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Mean ASR and GAP across attackers retain their existing reporting conventions; the table asterisks still indicate an ASR threshold rather than statistical significance.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports patched-trigger Acc/ASR of 92.40%/95.67% on CIFAR-10, 71.28%/96.06% on CIFAR-100, and 96.66%/94.63% on GTSRB. Figure 7 adds fluctuating ASR trajectories supporting mixed-method conflicts. Existing Tables 1–4, v2 Table 5 relocated as v3 Table 6, and retained plots preserve their results.

T1.justification: Despite its title, the new Appendix A.2 restates the overlapping-feature conflict intuition using classifier and feature-extractor notation; it adds no substantive formal result, derivation, or proof. The main equations retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, non-cooperative attack, ID-mapping, effectiveness, and persistence claims. The abstract still claims average ASR above 97% and ASR above 90% after 900 rounds; the appendix additions provide supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly characterizes the patched-trigger effect on ASR as slight but acceptable, refining v2's qualitative statement that pixel triggers remain effective. The conflict explanation and discussions of one-shot durability, model dependence, and potential defenses otherwise retain their meaning.

D1.justification: V3 specifies target classes 0, 1, and 2 and explains that static attacks share identical triggers for each attacker. The embedded code link changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. Conversely, Section 5 removes the explicit 0.001 PGD step size; this is lost documentation, not evidence of a changed value.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to BadFSS, BadCleaner, and FLPurifier and removes FLDetector. Its positioning relative to DBA and NBA remains substantively unchanged, with Appendix A.1 reiterating the existing distinction from NBA.

P1.justification: V3 makes grammatical corrections, simplifies notation, expands several explanations, and adds acknowledgments. New appendix sections precede and follow the retained supplementary material, whose headings and cross-references are updated. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the mixed-method ASR plot, patched-trigger table, and trigger/sample panels in Figures 9–11. Existing appendix displays are relocated and renumbered, and several retained figures are resized, particularly Figure 6. The main table structures and overall two-column design remain stable.

improvement.justification: The mixed-method conflict experiment and numerical patched-trigger results make existing claims better supported and easier to assess. Trigger examples and clarified settings also help readers. These modest gains outweigh the loss of the explicit PGD step size, although that omission and sparse setup information for Figure 7 limit the reproducibility improvement.
